question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\frac{1}{g},\,g=\operatorname{sinh}⁡s,\,s={x}^{3}
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}\cdot \frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g} & =-\frac{1}{{g}^{2}},\,\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}=\operatorname{cosh}⁡s,\,\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, multiplying the three results together and substituting for $g$ and $s$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{{g}^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡s\cdot 3{x}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡{x}^{3}}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{3}\cdot 3{x}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{3}}{{sinh}^{2}⁡{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
